header.userPrompt:
Make every code-producing built-in flow end with a best-effort pull request, and make the end-of-run branch handling follow the run target instead of a per-flow flag.

## Goal

Almost every built-in flow follows the same shape: understand (plan), code, review loop. Add a fourth, uniform final step: open a PR whenever the repository is detected to be on GitHub and GitHub is reachable. This is best effort: if it is not a GitHub repository, or GitHub cannot be reached / `gh` is not authenticated for that host, the flow says so in one line ("not a GitHub repository, no PR opened" / "cannot reach GitHub (<reason>), no PR opened") and finishes successfully without a PR. It must work for github.com and for self-hosted GitHub (GitHub Enterprise Server on any hostname).

## What to build

1. **GitHub detection built-in.** Add to the built-in tools (`GitHubTool`, `package orca.tools`) a read-only probe answering whether a PR can be opened from this checkout, as an enum, not booleans: e.g. `NoRemote`, `NotGitHub(host)`, `Unreachable(host, reason)` (gh not installed / not authenticated for that host / network), `Available(host, owner, repo)`. Derive the host from the `origin` remote URL (both ssh `git@host:path` and URL forms — `OsGitTool.remoteHost` already parses this; move or share it rather than duplicating). Treat github.com AND any host that `gh` recognises as a GitHub instance as GitHub — e.g. `gh auth status --hostname <host>` and/or `gh repo view --json owner,name` run against that host — do not hardcode github.com as the only GitHub host. Wire an `OsGitHubTool` implementation and a fake for tests.

2. **Self-hosted support in the existing PR code.** `OsGitHubTool.PrUrlPattern` and `PrHandle.url` hardcode `https://github.com/...`. Make them host-aware (e.g. `PrHandle` carries the host, or the URL is parsed generically by `<scheme>://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>`), so `createPr` / `findOpenPr` work on GHES. `PrHandle` travels through `JsonData` — no defaults on its fields (0.x rule in AGENTS.md).

3. **Best-effort PR helper in `orca.pr`.** Add a flow-level helper next to `openPrFromBranch` (e.g. `openPrIfGitHub(summarisingAgent = ..., ...)` returning `Option[PrHandle]`) that runs the probe first, and on anything but `Available` emits a single `OrcaEvent.Step` naming the reason and the next action, then returns `None`; on `Available` it pushes, summarises and creates the PR through the existing stages. The probe is a read and stays outside stages; push/summarise/create keep the existing three-stage split (resume safety — see `openPrFromBranch`'s scaladoc). Keep `openPrFromBranch` for flows that REQUIRE GitHub (the issue-driven ones), or implement it on top of the new one — one decision, one home.

4. **Branch handoff follows the run target.** Today `flow(..., returnToStartBranch: Boolean = false)` is a static per-flow choice, and `FlowLifecycle.finishBranch` acts on it. Replace that with a rule derived from `OrcaArgs.target` (`RunTarget`) and whether the run actually opened a PR — the invoking checkout should be left the way it was found:
   - `RunTarget.NewBranch`: when the flow opened a PR, check the start branch back out (the feature branch stays, pushed). When no PR was opened (not GitHub / unreachable), stay on the feature branch as today, so the user ends on the work; the closing summary already names the branch.
   - `RunTarget.Worktree`: never switch branches — the worktree stays on its `orca-worktree-<hash>` branch and the invoking checkout is untouched (already the case; keep it that way and make sure the PR step runs from inside the worktree).
   - `RunTarget.CurrentBranch` (`--skip-branch`): still push and open the PR best-effort from that branch, but never change what is checked out.
   Remove the `returnToStartBranch` parameter from `flow`/`runFlow`/`FlowLifecycle.run` and every call site (built-in flows, tests, README). The lifecycle needs to learn that a PR was opened: the PR helper records it on the flow context/control (a small, explicit door — no global mutable state; follow the capability conventions in AGENTS.md), and `teardownSuccess` reads it. The throwaway-branch deletion rule in `finishBranch` stays as is.

5. **Built-in flows.** Append the best-effort PR step to `flows/implement.sc`, `flows/implement-interactive.sc`, `flows/simple.sc`, and switch `flows/implement-enhanced.sc`, `flows/issue-pr.sc`, `flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc` off `returnToStartBranch = true`. The issue flows may keep requiring GitHub (they read the issue from it). `flows/review.sc` produces no code and gets no PR step. Update each flow's header comment and the one-line description on its first line. Note `orca create`/`orca fork` run `simple.sc` in a sandbox that is not a GitHub repo — the best-effort step must skip cleanly there (check `shell/.../create` for how the sandbox is set up and add/adjust a test if there is one).

6. **Docs and tests.** Update README ("The flow lifecycle" success-teardown paragraph, the built-in tools section, the flows/CLI sections mentioning PRs, any mention of `returnToStartBranch`) and AGENTS.md where the lifecycle description changes. Unit tests use the existing fakes (`StubCliRunner`, `TestFlowControl`, `orca.testkit.GitRepo`) — cover: the probe's enum outcomes from stubbed `gh`/`git` output (github.com, a GHES host, a non-GitHub host, no remote, gh unauthenticated); host-aware PR URL parsing; the helper's skip path emitting the reason; and `finishBranch` for each `RunTarget` × PR-opened/not. Run `sbt scalafmtAll`, `sbt compile` and `sbt test` (the full suite) before finishing; fix warnings under `-Wunused:all`. `ORCA_INTEGRATION=1 sbt publishLocal "shell/testOnly *BuiltInFlowsCompileTest"` compiles the built-in flows against the local build — run it, since the flow scripts change.

## Constraints

- Follow AGENTS.md: enums over booleans for modes, no defaults on persisted/domain fields, no back-compat shims, comments only for what the code cannot say, no history in comments, every user-facing refusal names the next action.
- Agents are trusted but fallible; do not justify any design by adversarial agent behaviour.
- Subprocess calls go through `CliRunner`/`QuietProc` (stderr captured), never raw `os.proc(...).call`.
- Do not commit-message-attribute anything to an AI; do not touch `.orca/settings.properties`.

resultJson.description:
Every code-producing built-in flow (implement, implement-interactive, simple, implement-enhanced) gains a uniform fourth step after plan → code → review: push the branch and open a pull request when the checkout's `origin` is a GitHub host (github.com, or a GitHub Enterprise Server host `gh` is logged in to) and `gh` can reach it. When it cannot — no remote, not GitHub, `gh` missing or unauthenticated — the flow says so in one `Step` line that names the next action and finishes successfully without a PR. The issue-driven flows (issue-pr, issue-pr-bugfix) keep requiring GitHub; review.sc produces no code and gets nothing.

Three runtime pieces support this. In `tools`, `GitHubTool` gets a read-only probe returning an enum (`NoRemote` / `NotGitHub(host)` / `Unreachable(host, reason)` / `Available(host, owner, repo)`), and `PrHandle` plus the `gh` URL parsing become host-aware so PR creation and lookup work on GHES. In `flow`, `orca.pr` gets `openPrIfGitHub` (probe outside stages, then the existing push → summarise → create stages) and a small explicit door on `FlowControl` through which the PR helpers record that a PR was opened. In `runner`, the static per-flow `returnToStartBranch` flag is removed everywhere; the success-teardown branch handoff is derived from `OrcaArgs.target` and whether a PR was opened: `NewBranch` + PR → return to the start branch (feature branch stays, pushed); `NewBranch` without PR → stay on the feature branch; `Worktree` and `CurrentBranch` → never switch. The throwaway-branch deletion rule is unchanged.

AGENTS.md constraints apply throughout: enums over booleans, no defaults on `JsonData` fields, no back-compat shims, every subprocess through `CliRunner`/`QuietProc`, comments state present-tense facts only, refusals name the next action, no design justified by adversarial agent behaviour. `orca create`/`orca fork` run `simple.sc` inside a sandbox repo with no remote, so the best-effort step must skip cleanly there.

tasks.title: Make PrHandle and the gh URL parsing host-aware
tasks.description: In `tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitHubTool.scala` change `PrHandle` to `PrHandle(host: String, owner: String, repo: String, number: Int) derives JsonData` (no defaults) with `url = s"https://$host/$owner/$repo/pull/$number"`; `shortRef` unchanged. Replace `OsGitHubTool.PrUrlPattern` with a generic `https?://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>` pattern and build the handle from all four groups in `createPr` and `findOpenPr`. Route every `PrHandle`-taking gh call to the handle's host: `--repo` becomes `<host>/<owner>/<repo>` (writeComment, buildStatus) and the `gh api` calls (readPrComments, updatePr, upsertComment's fetch/patch) gain `--hostname <host>`. Update every `PrHandle(...)` constructor: `OsGitHubToolTest`, `OsGitHubIntegrationTest`, `OpenPrFromBranchTest`, `FlowCompilesTest:261`, `flows/review.sc:104` (pass `"github.com"` explicitly), and the README `PrHandle` bullet (line 865). Tests in `OsGitHubToolTest`: `createPr` parses a github.com URL and a GHES URL (`https://ghe.example.com/acme/widgets/pull/42`) into handles carrying the host; `findOpenPr` (already-exists path) does the same; a PR-handle call passes `HOST/OWNER/REPO` to `--repo` and `--hostname HOST` to `gh api`; `PrHandle.url` renders the host. Run `sbt scalafmtAll`, `sbt compile`, `sbt test`.

tasks.title: Add the GitHub availability probe to GitHubTool
tasks.description: In `tools`: add `enum GitHubAvailability { case NoRemote; case NotGitHub(host: String); case Unreachable(host: String, reason: String); case Available(host: String, owner: String, repo: String) }` (public, `package orca.tools`) and `def availability(): GitHubAvailability` on the `GitHubTool` trait, documented as a read-only probe answering whether a PR can be opened from this checkout. Implement in `OsGitHubTool`: read `remote.origin.url` via `cli.run(Seq("git","config","--get","remote.origin.url"), env = OsGitTool.nonInteractiveEnv, cwd = workDir)` (non-zero → `NoRemote`); derive the host with `OsGitTool.remoteHost` (widen it to `private[tools]`; no host → `NotGitHub(url)`); run `gh auth status --hostname <host>`: success → `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` (new `private[tools]` DTO in `GhJson.scala`) → `Available(host, owner, repo)`; failure on `github.com` → `Unreachable(host, <trimmed gh stderr>)`; failure on any other host → `NotGitHub(host)`. A `NonFatal` exception from running `gh` (binary missing) → `Unreachable(host, "gh is not installed …")`. All calls go through `cli`. Add `GitHubAvailability` to the `orca.tools` export list in `runner/src/main/scala/orca/exports.scala`; implement `availability()` in `OpenPrFromBranchTest.RecordingGh`. Tests in `OsGitHubToolTest` with `SequencedCliRunner`: github.com origin + auth ok + repo view → `Available("github.com","acme","widgets")`; `git@ghe.example.com:acme/widgets.git` + auth ok → `Available` with that host; gitlab.com origin + auth failure → `NotGitHub("gitlab.com")`; `git config` exit 1 → `NoRemote`; github.com + `gh auth status` exit 1 → `Unreachable` carrying gh's stderr; a runner throwing on `gh` → `Unreachable` naming installation; the probe passes `--hostname <host>` to `gh auth status`. Run `sbt scalafmtAll`, `sbt compile`, `sbt test`.

tasks.title: Add the PR-opened door on FlowControl and the best-effort openPrIfGitHub helper
tasks.description: In `flow`: add a `private[orca] trait OpenedPrRecord` mixin (sibling of `StageFrames`; plain var documented as flow-thread-only per the `FlowControl` contract) providing `private[orca] def recordOpenedPr(pr: PrHandle): Unit` and `private[orca] def openedPr: Option[PrHandle]`; declare both abstract on `FlowControl`; mix the trait into `DefaultFlowContext` (runner), `TestFlowControl`, and `CommitMessageTest.FlowControlWithAgent`. In `openPrFromBranch.scala`: call `recordOpenedPr(handle)` after `stage("Open PR")` returns (runs on resume too, since the stage replays the handle); update its scaladoc to say it requires GitHub and point to `openPrIfGitHub`. Add `def openPrIfGitHub(summarisingAgent: Agent[?], title: PrSummary => String = _.title, body: PrSummary => String = _.body, context: Option[String] = None, instructions: String = PrPrompts.Summarise)(using FlowContext, FlowControl): Option[PrHandle]` in a new `orca.pr` file: call `gh.availability()` OUTSIDE any stage; on `Available` return `Some(openPrFromBranch(...))`; otherwise emit exactly one `OrcaEvent.Step` and return `None`, e.g. `no git remote, no PR opened — add a GitHub origin to have orca open one`, `not a GitHub repository (origin is <host>), no PR opened — if it is a GitHub Enterprise host, run gh auth login --hostname <host> and re-run`, `cannot reach GitHub (<reason>), no PR opened — <next action>`. Add a public `def recordOpenedPr(pr: PrHandle)(using FlowControl): Unit` in `orca.pr` (scaladoc: tells the lifecycle a PR was opened so a new-branch run returns to its start branch; the two helpers call it themselves). Export `openPrIfGitHub` and `recordOpenedPr` from `exports.scala`. Tests in `flow/src/test/scala/orca/pr/OpenPrIfGitHubTest.scala`, reusing `OpenPrFromBranchTest`'s fakes (extract shared ones if cleaner): for each of `NoRemote`, `NotGitHub`, `Unreachable` the helper returns `None`, emits no `StageStarted`, calls neither `push` nor `createPr`, emits one `Step` containing "no PR opened" and the reason, and `openedPr` stays `None`; for `Available` it returns `Some(handle)`, runs the three stages, and `openedPr == Some(handle)`; `openPrFromBranch` alone records the handle. Run `sbt scalafmtAll`, `sbt compile`, `sbt test`.

tasks.title: Derive the end-of-run branch handoff from the run target and the opened PR
tasks.description: In `runner`: add `private[runner] enum BranchHandoff { case ReturnToStart, StayPut }` with `BranchHandoff.of(target: RunTarget, worktree: Option[os.Path], openedPr: Option[PrHandle]): BranchHandoff` — `ReturnToStart` only for `RunTarget.NewBranch(_)` with `worktree.isEmpty` and a PR opened; everything else `StayPut` (scaladoc states the per-target rules). Remove `returnToStartBranch` from `flow(...)` and `runFlow(...)`; `FlowLifecycle.run(ctx, flowSetup, target: RunTarget, debug)` computes `BranchHandoff.of(target, flowSetup.worktree, ctx.openedPr)` after the body succeeds and passes it to `teardownSuccess(git, setup, handoff: BranchHandoff, emit)` → `finishBranch(git, setup, handoff)`; keep the throwaway-delete rule; update both scaladocs without history wording. Delete the `returnToStartBranch = true` argument and its comment from `flows/implement-enhanced.sc`, `flows/issue-pr.sc`, `flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc` (bodies unchanged here). Update every runner test call site (`runFlowForTest`, direct `runFlow`/`flow`/`teardownSuccess`/`closingSummary` calls, `FlowContextAgentTest`, `RoleSettingsFlowTest`, `LeadAgentIdentityTest`) and the `ClosingSummaryTest:42` comment. Tests: `BranchHandoff.of` over the full product — NewBranch/CurrentBranch/Worktree × {PR, no PR}, plus NewBranch+PR with `worktree = Some(...)` → `StayPut`; `finishBranch` with `ReturnToStart` checks out the start branch and keeps the feature branch, with `StayPut` leaves HEAD on the feature branch, throwaway still deletes; end-to-end through `runFlowForTest` (give it a `gh` parameter feeding `FlowWiring(gh = ...)`) with a fake whose `availability()` is `Available` and `createPr` returns a handle, body calling `openPrIfGitHub`: HEAD ends on `main` with the feature branch kept; a `NotGitHub` fake leaves HEAD on the feature branch; a `CurrentBranch` run with a PR opened stays on its branch. Replace the two README mentions of `returnToStartBranch` (flow-methods row at 279, success-teardown bullet at 369–377) with the target-derived rule. Run `sbt scalafmtAll`, `sbt compile`, `sbt test`.

tasks.title: Append the best-effort PR step to the built-in flows
tasks.description: Append `openPrIfGitHub(summarisingAgent = codingAgent.cheap)` as the last statement of `flows/implement.sc`, `flows/implement-interactive.sc`, `flows/simple.sc`; switch `flows/implement-enhanced.sc` from `openPrFromBranch` to `openPrIfGitHub`; keep `openPrFromBranch` in `flows/issue-pr.sc`; in `flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc` call `recordOpenedPr(pr)` right after the `"Push + open tentative PR"` stage (outside the stage); leave `flows/review.sc`. Update each changed flow's first-line description and header scaladoc to state the final step ("then opens a PR when the repository is on GitHub; otherwise says so and ends on the feature branch") and the `gh` wording (optional for the best-effort flows, required for the issue flows); in `simple.sc` note that under `orca create`/`orca fork` the sandbox has no remote so the step skips. In `BuiltInFlowsTest` pin that exactly `implement-enhanced.sc`, `implement-interactive.sc`, `implement.sc`, `simple.sc` contain `openPrIfGitHub(`, that `issue-pr.sc` contains `openPrFromBranch(` and `issue-pr-bugfix.sc` contains `recordOpenedPr(`, and that no flow mentions `returnToStartBranch`. In `AuthoringSandboxTest` add one test pinning that the sandbox has no remote (`git remote` output empty), with a comment that this is what makes the authoring flow's PR step skip. Run `sbt scalafmtAll`, `sbt test`, then `ORCA_INTEGRATION=1 sbt publishLocal "shell/testOnly *BuiltInFlowsCompileTest"` and report its result verbatim.

tasks.title: Document the best-effort PR step and the target-derived handoff
tasks.description: README: extend the "Built-in tools" `gh` row with `availability` (the four cases, one phrase each; github.com and GHES); add `gh.availability` to the pure-reads list in "Side effects happen inside stages"; in the PR utilities table (~780) add rows for `openPrIfGitHub(summarisingAgent, title?, body?, context?, instructions?)` (probe, then push → summarise → create; one `Step` and `None` when not on GitHub / unreachable), `openPrFromBranch(...)` (requires GitHub), and `recordOpenedPr(pr)`; rewrite the implement.sc intro (146–150) so it says the flow ends by opening a PR when the repo is on GitHub and otherwise leaves you on the feature branch; note in the `orca create` row (~977) that the sandbox has no remote, so no PR is opened. ADR 0018: add a `> **Amendment (2026-09-11).**` block under R3 stating the handoff is derived from `RunTarget` and whether a PR was opened, without rewriting the original text. AGENTS.md needs no change unless a grep finds `returnToStartBranch` there. Keep sentences short and factual. Run `sbt test` (BuiltInFlowsTest reads flow text) and grep the repo for `returnToStartBranch` — only ADR text and `docs/` history files may still mention it.

## Modules and where things live

- `tools/` — tool traits + os-backed impls. `tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitHubTool.scala` holds `PrHandle` (line 17, `derives JsonData`), `IssueHandle`, the `GitHubTool` trait (178) and `private[orca] class OsGitHubTool(cli: CliRunner, workDir, pollInterval, events: OrcaListener, readRetry)` (265) with companion. `GitTool.scala` holds `GitTool`/`OsGitTool`; `GhJson.scala` holds the `private[tools] case class ... derives ConfiguredJsonValueCodec` wire DTOs (list codecs are `private[orca] given` at the bottom).
- `flow/` — `flow/src/main/scala/orca/pr/{openPrFromBranch,summarisePr,PrPrompts,orcaCommentMarker}.scala`; `FlowContext.scala`, `FlowControl.scala` (trait with a `captureChecking` import; extends `caps.ExclusiveCapability`; all members abstract), `StageFrames.scala` (the `private[orca] trait` mixin every `FlowControl` impl shares for per-run bookkeeping; owner-thread assert pattern lives there), `Flow.scala` (`stage`), `RuntimeInStage.scala` (the only production mint of `InStage`/`WorkspaceWrite`).
- `runner/` — `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala` (`flow(...)` at 132, `private[orca] runFlow(...)` at 296, both carry `returnToStartBranch: Boolean`; `runFlow` has `args: OrcaArgs` in hand), `orca/RunTarget.scala` (`enum RunTarget { NewBranch(uncommitted), CurrentBranch(uncommitted), Worktree }`), `orca/OrcaArgs.scala` (`OrcaArgs(userPrompt, verbose, target: RunTarget)`), `orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala` (`run(ctx, flowSetup, returnToStartBranch, debug)` at 67 → `teardownSuccess(git, setup, returnToStartBranch, emit)` at 1152 → `finishBranch(git, setup, returnToStartBranch)(using WorkspaceWrite)` at 1217; `FlowSetup` at 225 with `featureBranch: FeatureBranch`, `startBranch: String`, `branchMode: BranchMode` (Created/Reused), `worktree: Option[os.Path]`), `orca/runner/DefaultFlowContext.scala` (production `FlowControl`, mixes `StageFrames`), `orca/runner/ClosingSummary.scala`, `orca/exports.scala` (re-export surface: line 48 exports `orca.pr.*` names, line 80 exports `orca.tools.*` names — new public names go there).
- `shell/` — `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/AuthorAction.scala` runs the built-in `simple.sc` with `RunTarget.NewBranch(Uncommitted.Stash)` inside `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/create/AuthoringSandbox.scala` (`git init` temp dir, one root commit, NO remote). Tests: `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/create/AuthoringSandboxTest.scala`, `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/flows/BuiltInFlowsTest.scala` (pins flow script text via resources, e.g. the `taskBasedFlows` exact-set pins), `BuiltInFlowsCompileTest` (ORCA_INTEGRATION-gated, compiles the scripts against a `publishLocal`).
- `flows/*.sc` — first line is a one-line `//` description (shown by the shell), then `//> using` directives, then a `/** ... */` header. `import orca.{*, given}` brings in everything `exports.scala` exports.

## Existing code to build on (exact facts)

- `PrHandle(owner: String, repo: String, number: Int)`; `url = s"https://github.com/$owner/$repo/pull/$number"`; `shortRef = owner/repo#number`. `OsGitHubTool.PrUrlPattern = """https://github\.com/([^/]+)/([^/]+)/pull/(\d+)""".r` (line 287), used by `createPr` (315) and `findOpenPr` (376, over `GhPrListJson.url`; `GhJson.scala`'s doc for that DTO names `[[PrUrlPattern]]`). Methods taking a `PrHandle` pass `--repo s"${pr.owner}/${pr.repo}"` (writeComment 440, buildStatus 527) or `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/...` (readPrComments 411, updatePr 427, fetchIdentifiedComments 502, patchComment 517). gh facts: `--repo` accepts `HOST/OWNER/REPO`; `gh api --hostname HOST ...` targets a GHES host; `gh auth status --hostname HOST` exits 0 only when logged in to that host (a token in `GH_TOKEN` counts); `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` resolves the repo from the cwd's git remotes on any host gh is logged in to. `PrHandle(...)` constructors to update: `tools/src/test/.../OsGitHubToolTest.scala:68`, `OsGitHubIntegrationTest.scala:36`, `flow/src/test/.../OpenPrFromBranchTest.scala:66,179`, `runner/src/test/scala/flowtests/FlowCompilesTest.scala:261`, `flows/review.sc:104` (builds a `PrHandle` from an `IssueHandle`, whose parser only accepts github.com URLs — pass `"github.com"` explicitly there), README line 865. The only `GitHubTool` fake in the repo is `OpenPrFromBranchTest.RecordingGh`.
- `OsGitTool.remoteHost(url): Option[String]` (GitTool.scala:1226, currently `private`) parses both `git@host:path` and `scheme://[user@]host[:port]/path`; `isGithubRemote` (1234) is its only caller; tested in `OsGitToolTest.scala:358`. Widen to `private[tools]` and reuse. `OsGitTool.nonInteractiveEnv` (1215, `private[tools]`) must be passed as `env` to any git subprocess. `OsGitHubTool.headBranchForPr` (346) shows running git through the tool's own `cli`: `cli.run(Seq("git", ...), env = OsGitTool.nonInteractiveEnv, cwd = workDir)`. `git config --get remote.origin.url` exits 1 when unset.
- `CliRunner.run(args, stdin = "", env = Map.empty, cwd = os.pwd): CliResult(exitCode, stdout, stderr)`. A missing binary makes `os.proc` throw from `run` — catch `NonFatal` in the probe. `OsGitHubTool.runGhResult(args*)` (581) is the raw funnel; `ghRead` retries, `ghMutate` doesn't; `fail(label, result)` throws `OrcaFlowException`.
- `openPrFromBranch(summarisingAgent: Agent[?], title: PrSummary => String = _.title, body: PrSummary => String = _.body, context: Option[String] = None, instructions: String = PrPrompts.Summarise)(using FlowContext, FlowControl): PrHandle` — three stages "Push branch" / "Generate PR title and description" / "Open PR". `git.defaultBase()` THROWS when the repo has no remote, so the probe must run before the summarise stage. `stage(...)` replays a recorded result on resume, so code placed after `stage("Open PR")` still runs (with the replayed handle) on a resumed run.
- `FlowControl` implementations: `DefaultFlowContext` (runner), `TestFlowControl` (`flow/src/test/scala/orca/TestFlowContext.scala:70`, with `TestFlowControl.create(dispatcher, ...)` returning `(control, repoDir)` over `GitRepo.seeded()`), `CommitMessageTest.FlowControlWithAgent` (`flow/src/test/scala/orca/CommitMessageTest.scala:61`). `FlowLifecycleTest.StubFlowContext` (4102) implements only `FlowContext`, so a new `FlowControl` member does not touch it.
- Test fakes: `StubCliRunner(initialResponse)` (`tools/src/test/scala/orca/subprocess/StubCliRunner.scala`, one canned response, `setResponse`, records `calls`); `OsGitHubToolTest.SequencedCliRunner(responses)` (private to that suite, returns responses in turn, last repeats, records calls). `OpenPrFromBranchTest` has a recording `GitHubTool` fake (`RecordingGh`), a `RecordingGit` delegating to a real `OsGitTool` via `export` while stubbing `push`/`defaultBase`/`diffVsBase`, a `StubSummariser` agent, and `PrTestControl extends TestFlowControl` overriding `lazy val gh`. Listener capture: `val listener: OrcaListener = { case OrcaEvent.Step(m) => ...; case _ => () }`.
- Runner test seams: `FlowLifecycleTest.runFlowForTest(workDir, prompt, store, extraListeners)(body)` (1762) hardcodes `wiring = FlowWiring(claude = Some(_ => StubAgent.claude))` and `returnToStartBranch = false`; `FlowWiring` also has a `gh: Option[GitHubTool]` slot. A worktree-run fixture exists around line 211 (`runFlowForTest(worktree, prompt, store)`). Existing handoff tests: "success teardown ... stays on feature branch" (~1880) and "success teardown with returnToStartBranch=true returns to start, keeps branch" (1929, uses `flow(...)` directly). Direct `teardownSuccess` tests at 3143–3187; `closingSummary(git, setup, returnToStartBranch)` helper at 3192 and `closingSetup(...)` at 3206 (builds a `FlowSetup` with `worktree = None`). Other `returnToStartBranch = false` occurrences to delete: `FlowLifecycleTest` (many), `FlowContextAgentTest:32`, `RoleSettingsFlowTest:489`, `LeadAgentIdentityTest:168,235`.

resultJson.body:
## Summary

Every code-producing built-in flow now ends with a best-effort PR step: when the repository is on GitHub and `gh` can reach it, the flow pushes the branch and opens a PR; when it can't—no remote, not GitHub, `gh` unreachable—the flow reports why in one line and finishes successfully without a PR.

The per-flow `returnToStartBranch` flag is gone. The run now decides where to leave the checkout: a `NewBranch` run that opened a PR hands you back the branch you started on (the work is on the PR); every other run stays put.

## What changed

**Tools:** Added `gh.availability()`, a read-only probe answering whether a PR can be opened as a `GitHubAvailability` enum (Available / NoRemote / NoHost / NotGitHub / Unreachable). Made `PrHandle` carry the host as its first field so PR creation, lookup, and writes work on GitHub Enterprise Server. Derived the host from the `origin` remote URL via the existing `remoteHost` parser.

**Flow runtime:** Extracted the three stages of `openPrFromBranch` (push → summarise → create) into private helpers. Added `openPrIfGitHub`, which probes first and either runs those stages or emits one Step naming the reason and returns None. Added a small explicit door on `FlowControl`—`recordOpenedPr`—so a flow that opens its PR with a bare `gh.createPr` can tell the lifecycle. Added `BranchHandoff.of(target, worktree, openedPr)` to compute the checkout location: ReturnToStart only for NewBranch runs outside a worktree that opened a PR; everything else stays put.

**Built-in flows:** Appended `openPrIfGitHub(codingAgent.cheap)` to implement.sc, implement-interactive.sc, and simple.sc. Switched implement-enhanced.sc from `openPrFromBranch` to `openPrIfGitHub`. Kept `openPrFromBranch` in issue-pr.sc (those flows require GitHub); added `recordOpenedPr` to issue-pr-bugfix.sc so the lifecycle learns about its tentative PR. Removed `returnToStartBranch` arguments and updated flow headers to describe the new behavior.

**Docs:** Updated README to document `gh.availability`, the new PR helper signatures, the host-aware `PrHandle`, and the target-derived branch handoff rule. Added a dated amendment to ADR 0018 R3. Updated AGENTS.md to list the new test fakes.

The PR step runs outside a worktree by construction; `orca create`/`orca fork` run simple.sc in a sandbox with no remote, so the step skips cleanly there.

(2) `PrHandle` carries `host` as its first field; `url` is `https://<host>/...`; PR-handle-taking gh calls route to `pr.host`. `IssueHandle` stays github.com-only. (3) The recording door is `private[orca]` on `FlowControl`; `openPrFromBranch` calls it after its "Open PR" stage, `openPrIfGitHub` is built on `openPrFromBranch`, and a public `recordOpenedPr(pr)(using FlowControl)` in `orca.pr` (exported) exists for scripts that call `gh.createPr` directly. (4) The handoff is a two-case runner enum computed in one place from `(target, setup.worktree, openedPr)`.
